items.title: The nearby-open quasi-section conclusion survives replacing quasi-finiteness by local finite type plus a closed point in the fibre
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma swaps the hypotheses of the chapter's quasi-section lemma (lemma-quasi-finite-quasi-section-meeting-nearby-open-X) for weaker-looking but equivalent-for-the-purpose ones: f : X -> S locally of finite type with S locally Noetherian, x a closed point of its fibre X_s, U an open missing the fibre through x with x in the closure of U; then the conclusions of the cited quasi-finite lemma hold. The retained proof is a written reduction: shrink X and S to affine neighbourhoods of x and s, so X is Noetherian (cited Morphisms lemma finite-type-noetherian and the two Topology lemmas that Noetherian spaces are quasi-compact), hence U is quasi-compact, and the scheme-theoretic-image lemma (Morphisms, lemma reach-points-scheme-theoretic-image) supplies a specialization x' -> x with x' in U; the image point of x' differs from s, so the original quasi-finite-lemma hypotheses at (x', f(x')) are met and the reduction is justified line by line. Retained author proof at lines 15063-15075.
